work_order.understanding: Issue #71 carries one non-blocking review finding from PR #70: the last case in app/groups/[id]/transfer-line-wrap.test.ts (lines 73-90) asserts on the wording of a JSX comment above the transfer-row name wrapper (must contain 'min-w-0', must not contain 'ml-auto' or a newline). It is prose, not markup, so a legitimate rewording of the comment fails CI with no behaviour change. The finding still reproduces on main: the case is present and page.tsx:547 holds the one-line comment it pins. The reviewer's own stated fix is 'drop it rather than loosening it'. The inner name span's classes (min-w-0, break-words, tone, body type), the amount span's classes and the single transferWords call site are pinned by the four earlier cases, which stay. The outer name wrapper (page.tsx:548) is not pinned by any case, before or after this change.
work_order.approach: Delete the fifth `it(...)` block ("keeps the comment above the name wrapper ...") from transfer-line-wrap.test.ts and nothing else. Do not touch page.tsx: the comment stays as written, merely no longer test-pinned. The file's header doc comment describes the classes, not the comment case, so it stays accurate. Loosening the assertion is not done because a case that still greps comment prose has the same defect; deleting follows the finding's own instruction. Adding a new assertion for the outer wrapper's min-w-0 is deliberately left out: that gap pre-dates this change and the ticket is a one-finding cleanup.

files.change: Remove the last `it("keeps the comment above the name wrapper to one line about min-w-0 and not the amount's ml-auto", ...)` block (lines 73-90) and the blank line before it, leaving the describe closing `});` intact. The four remaining cases and the helpers (CALL, pageSource, spanClasses, nameClasses, amountClasses) are all still used and unchanged.
files.why: The case pins comment wording, so rewording the comment fails CI without any behaviour change; the reviewer recommended dropping it.

cases: lets the name span shrink and break (kept)
keeps the direction tone and body type on the name (kept)
keeps the amount right-aligned, tabular and toned when the name takes the line (kept)
renders the transfer words at exactly one site (kept)
comment-wording case removed: no remaining assertion reads text inside a JSX comment

acceptance.check: The comment-wording case is gone from transfer-line-wrap.test.ts and the file's remaining four cases pass.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Run `npx vitest run app/groups` (or the file's path) and confirm the output reports 4 tests passed for transfer-line-wrap.test.ts, not 'no tests found'. The file no longer contains `indexOf('{/*'` or `.not.toContain('ml-auto')`, and its title 'keeps the comment above the name wrapper' is absent.

acceptance.check: Rewording the comment at page.tsx:547 (for example making it two lines or mentioning ml-auto) no longer fails any test, while removing min-w-0 or break-words from the inner name span still does.
acceptance.how_to_verify: Temporarily reword the comment at page.tsx:547 and run the file: green. Temporarily remove `min-w-0` from the className at page.tsx:550 (the span around transferWords): the 'lets the name span shrink and break' case fails. Revert both. (The outer wrapper at page.tsx:548 is not covered by any case; do not use it for this check.)

acceptance.check: No production file changed and the verify suite is green.
acceptance.how_to_verify: `git diff --stat` shows only transfer-line-wrap.test.ts; `npm run typecheck && npm run test:ci` pass.

alternatives_considered.approach: Loosen the case: keep the min-w-0 check but drop the newline and ml-auto assertions.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: It still asserts on comment prose, so rewording that omits the phrase fails CI; the reviewer said to drop it rather than loosen it, and the markup is covered by the class cases.

alternatives_considered.approach: Delete the comment from page.tsx and the case together.
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: The comment explains a non-obvious fact (overflow-wrap cannot lower a flex item's min-content floor) that conventions.md also records; removing it is a production-file change the finding does not ask for.

alternatives_considered.approach: Replace the case with a markup assertion on the outer name wrapper's classes (page.tsx:548, min-w-0 flex-wrap).
alternatives_considered.rejected_because: Sound in itself and the critique's suggestion, but it is a new test for a gap that existed before #70 and is not what this finding asks; it would turn a pure deletion into new test design. Recorded as a residual risk instead.

assumptions: The case was added in #70 only to guard the comment's wording, not to prove any rendered behaviour.
Nothing else references the deleted case by name (the proposer's grep found only the case itself).
Memory is the Librarian's and is not edited here.
unknowns: Whether a later ticket intends to re-pin comment wording; none visible in the repo.
risks: The comment's one-line form is no longer enforced, so a future edit could grow it back to two lines or reintroduce the misleading ml-auto mention; cosmetic and accepted per the review's severity.
No .sdlc/memory edit is proposed (reserved to the Librarian) even though conventions/qa notes might mention the case.
out_of_scope: Any change to app/groups/[id]/page.tsx, including the comment text.
A test pinning min-w-0 on the outer name wrapper at page.tsx:548: no case reads that span today (nameClasses resolves to the inner span), a gap that pre-dates this change.
Pixel-width proof at 375px, which the file header already says is a browser concern.
evidence: transfer-line-wrap.test.ts:73-90 is the comment-wording case; it reads source.indexOf('{/*', li) and asserts contains 'min-w-0', not contains '\n', not contains 'ml-auto'.
page.tsx:547 holds the one-line comment directly above the outer name wrapper span at :548, so the finding reproduces on main.

page.tsx:550 (inner span, min-w-0 break-words) and :565 (amount, ml-auto tabular-nums) carry the classes asserted by cases 1-3; nameClasses() uses lastIndexOf('<span', call of transferWords) which resolves to the inner span at :549, confirming the outer wrapper at :548 is unread.
transfer-line-wrap.test.ts:10 (file header) also mentions ml-auto, so a literal grep for it still hits after the deletion.
work_order.confidence_rationale: Single-file deletion of one test block, finding verified present on main, the reviewer's own recommended fix, no production code or callers involved. The only soft spot is judgement: whether to also pin the outer wrapper, which I chose not to; a reviewer who wants that would move this, not the correctness of the deletion.
work_order.debate_summary: The critic called the proposal 'sound' but raised one major and two minor findings. Major (outer wrapper's min-w-0 unpinned, so 'the four other cases cover all class behaviour' is false): upheld on the facts - I re-read page.tsx:543-565 and the helpers, and cases 1-2 read only the inner span. But I rejected the proposed remedy of adding a new assertion in this ticket: the gap pre-dates #70, the deleted case never asserted that class either (it read only comment text), and the finding being fixed says to drop the case. I corrected the claim in the work order's understanding and recorded the gap in out_of_scope and residual_risks instead of widening the diff. Minor 1 (AC-1's grep for ml-auto is inexact because the file header also mentions it): upheld, AC-1 reworded. Minor 2 (AC-2 must name the inner span): upheld, AC-2 now names page.tsx:550. The bracketed-path 'no tests found' edge case is folded into AC-1. No decision in the brief applied; none was recorded.
residual_risks: The outer name wrapper's min-w-0 and flex-wrap (page.tsx:548) are asserted by no test, before or after this change: removing them passes CI while a long name could widen the page at 375px. QA should check it in a browser if it walks the layout.
The comment at page.tsx:547 is no longer pinned and may drift back to two lines or mention ml-auto.
qa_script: No UI change: no browser walk is needed. Run `npx vitest run app/groups/[id]/transfer-line-wrap.test.ts` and confirm 4 passed (not 'no tests found').

issue_snapshot.title: Follow-ups from #69: 1 from the review
issue_snapshot.body:
What the review and QA of PR #70 (for #69) found and did not fix there — filed as it merged, one ticket for the lot.

## From the review

Non-blocking findings the reviewer approved despite: a statement about severity, not a judgement that they are wrong.

### The new case pins the wording of a JSX comment (must contain 'min-w-0', must not contain 'ml-auto' or a newline), so a legitimate rewording of the comment fails CI without any behaviour change.

> The new case pins the wording of a JSX comment (must contain 'min-w-0', must not contain 'ml-auto' or a newline), so a legitimate rewording of the comment fails CI without any behaviour change.
> 
> `app/groups/[id]/transfer-line-wrap.test.ts:73`
> 
> Evidence: Ran the case's anchors by hand on main's page.tsx: comment spans two lines and contains ml-auto (case would fail); on the PR's page.tsx it is one line, min-w-0, no ml-auto (passes). The case asserts on prose, not on markup, which the existing cases already cover.
> 
> Fix: Acceptable as shipped because the work order chose it deliberately and the plan review required a CI proof; if it becomes a nuisance, drop it rather than loosening it.

---

**Check each one still reproduces before planning it.** They were written against the PR as it stood, and a later round can have fixed one. Some may not hold up: say so and drop them rather than implementing something that was never wrong. Split this if they turn out to be unrelated.

Depends on #69.
